title: Disaster Recovery Runbooks & RTO / RPO
description: Design Disaster Recovery (DR) plans, meet RTO and RPO metrics, and execute multi-region failover tests.

data.text: A database high-availability architecture is useless without documented, tested Disaster Recovery (DR) runbooks. DR strategy is defined by two fundamental metrics: **RTO** and **RPO**.

rows: How long can the application be down before recovery?
How much data loss (in time) is acceptable?

items.text: Automated WAL segment shipping to offsite cold storage (S3/GCS)
items.hint: Protects against entire data center destruction

items.text: Quarterly game day drills testing database recovery from scratch
Documented runbook with explicit DNS/connection string failover steps
items.hint: Do not invent failover steps during an outage

items.text: Alerts for replication lag exceeding 10 seconds

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: RTO measures downtime duration; RPO measures data loss window.
Regular game day recovery rehearsals are mandatory.
Offsite WAL archiving guarantees data survival even if the primary cloud region fails.
